title: Killings blamed on lack of shrinks
article: A 2022 killing spree by a man with mental health issues was "largely the result of a lack of adequate external monitoring" due to a severe shortage of psychiatrists in Laval, a coroner's inquest heard Wednesday. The assessment was in a letter Dr. Simon Roussel, a psychiatrist, wrote to officials at Laval's regional health authority on Aug. 4, 2022. That was the day Abdulla Shaikh, 26, was killed by police in a shootout after killing three strangers.

Shaikh, who suffered from schizophrenia, was hospitalized three times in the psychiatric ward at Laval's Cité-de-la-Santé Hospital. "Once again ... a psychiatric patient, who was probably not adequately followed, is making headlines after having killed three people in two days in Laval and Montreal," Roussel wrote in the letter, part of the evidence at the inquest. Coroner Géhane Kamel is investigating the four deaths. Her role is to identify contributing factors and come up with "recommendations to better protect human life."

Shaikh wasn't one of Roussel's patients. But Roussel said that in July 2022 one of his own patients sparked a major police operation requiring the deployment of 18 officers, as well as the tactical squad. Roussel was on leave at the time. "His followup had not been adequately ensured for several months, despite numerous rehospitalizations," Roussel said. "In my opinion, these incidents are largely the result of a lack of adequate external monitoring, due to a major shortage of psychiatrists." The inquest's public hearings are scheduled to continue until mid-October.
